brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1666456 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 8.8s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 37% over 30s (68/108 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $11,585/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 1666456) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $11,585/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: The blocking workload (adhoc_reporting) is not in the workload registry (BIZ-2), so its cost of interruption is unknown. The trade-off cannot be computed. Additionally, the change calendar has not been checked for owner consent policy. These must be resolved before a decision can be made.

audit.report: The checkout subsystem degraded after an unknown workload acquired a lock on session pid 1666456 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting), which has been idle in transaction for over 8 seconds. Twelve sessions are currently waiting on locks, and checkout success has dropped to 37% over the last 30 seconds, putting approximately $11,585/min in revenue at risk. The business tolerance for degraded checkout is 60 seconds, but the negotiation was escalated after 39.5 seconds because the Database Guardian could not ground its decision without evidence from the workload registry and change calendar. The business is currently unrecovered and awaiting escalation resolution.
audit.root_cause: An unknown workload (adhoc_reporting) holds a lock on session pid 1666456, blocking 12 sessions and causing checkout to degrade to 37% success.
lessons: Add adhoc_reporting to the workload registry immediately so the cost of interruption can be computed during future lock contention events.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian repeatedly proposed 'wait' based on the 60s business tolerance and the 8.8s idle time of the blocker, but the Continuity Guardian could not ground the review because adhoc_reporting was absent from the workload registry and the change calendar was not checked, causing two grounding failures and an escalation after 39.5 seconds.
follow_ups: Populate the workload registry for adhoc_reporting with owner and cost information.
Instruct the on-call to review the change calendar for adhoc_reporting and confirm whether any pending changes affect lock behavior.
After resolution, run a post-incident drill to test that the orchestrator escalates when grounding evidence is missing rather than timing out.

events.title: No relevant memories (searched 12)
R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 1666456) has been idle for only 4.3s. Waiting allows the transaction to complete naturally without terminating a session that may be part of a larger batch process. The business tolerance is 60s of degraded checkout; the current timeout window (10s verification) has not yet been exceeded. No evidence suggests terminating adhoc_reporting was verified ineffective in memory.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker's transaction commits within the wait period, the 12 waiting checkout sessions will acquire their locks and checkout success will recover. If the transaction rolls back or runs longer, checkout will continue to timeout.
proposal.risk_assessment: The blocker may hold locks for longer than the 60s business tolerance, causing sustained checkout failures and revenue at risk. Terminating the blocker risks interrupting a batch workload that may have downstream effects not yet observed.
